items.title: The General (1926)
items.synopsis: I've been researching newly public domain films from 1929 and earlier, so I'm uploading the best possible copies that I can find. One of the most acclaimed silent films to this day, The General is known as Buster Keaton's finest film. Based on the memoirs of a union soldier, this film follows a engineer as he fights to save his train. With dangerous stunts, a cute romance, and a likeable lead, The General is now thought of as a masterpiece. This wasn't always the case, however. On release reviews were poor and the box office barely recouped its investment, leading to Buster Keaton losing independence as a filmmaker.

items.title: The Passion Of Joan Of Arc (1928) FRENCH
items.synopsis: Carl Theodor Dreyer’s silent masterpiece (1928) dramatizes the 1431 trial and execution of Joan of Arc, drawing on the actual court transcripts. Renée Jeanne Falconetti stars as Joan in one of cinema’s most celebrated performances. Her interrogation by a panel of clerics, including Pierre Cauchon (Eugène Silvain) and Jean d’Estivet (Maurice Schutz), plays out in extreme close-ups, with Antonin Artaud as the sympathetic monk Jean Massieu. Rudolph Maté was the cinematographer, and Hermann Warm designed the sets. A Société Générale des Films production, filmed in Paris and released in France in 1928. Dreyer’s original negative was believed destroyed by fire. A copy of his original cut was found

items.title: The Last Laugh (1924)
items.synopsis: English Subtitles The Last Laugh (German: Der letzte Mann, transl. The Last Man) is a 1924 German silent film directed by German director F. W. Murnau from a screenplay written by Carl Mayer. The film stars Emil Jannings and Maly Delschaft. Stephen Brockmann summarized the film's plot as, "a nameless hotel doorman loses his job”. It is a cinematic example of the Kammerspielfilm or "chamber-drama" genre, which follows the style of short, sparse plays of lower middle-class life that emphasized the psychology of the characters rather than the sets and action. items.title: Fantasmagorie (1908)
items.synopsis: Fantasmagorie (1908) is a landmark silent animated film created by French artist and filmmaker Émile Cohl. Released in France in 1908, it is widely regarded by film historians as one of the earliest examples of fully hand-drawn animation in cinema history. The film consists of a continuous sequence of rapidly transforming line drawings, produced frame by frame through traditional hand animation techniques. Its surreal structure features constantly changing figures and objects that shift, dissolve, and reform without a conventional narrative, reflecting the experimental spirit of early cinema. The distinctive “chalk-line” visual style was achieved through photographic reversal of ink drawings

items.title: Mutt And Jeff Cartoons
items.synopsis: Mutt and Jeff was a long-running and widely popular American newspaper comic strip created by cartoonist Bud Fisher in 1907. It's commonly regarded as the first daily comic strip. Mutt and Jeff starred in in 292 animated shorts, making it the longest-running theatrical animated short series of the silent era, second to Krazy Kat in terms of years. The series ran from 1916 to 1923 and 1925-1926. Sadly very few of these films survive today.

items.title: Reefer Madness (1936) [HQ]
items.synopsis: Reefer Madness (original title: Tell Your Children) is an American public service announcement and exploitation film about drug use and abuse, specifically marijuana. It was financed by a church group and intended to be shown to parents as a morality tale about the dangers of cannabis use. It was inspired by the case of Victor Licata, who killed his father, mother, two brothers, and a sister with an ax in Tampa, allegedly while under the influence of marijuana.

It stars Gregory Walcott, Mona McKinnon, Tor Johnson, and "Vampira" (Maila Nurmi) and is narrated by Criswell. It also posthumously bills Bela Lugosi as a guest-star (silent footage of the actor had been shot by Wood for another, unfinished film just prior to Lugosi's death in August 1956). Other guest-stars are Hollywood veterans Lyle Talbot, who claimed that he never refused any acting job, and former cowboy star Tom Keene.
